items.title: Complete the canonical capability rule and add the forge-0-epic pointer
items.description:
Two canon edits, one commit, plus full adapter regeneration.

1. `references/stage-exit-protocol.md` § "Host and capability determination": this section states clauses **a** and **b** today. Add the paragraph specified verbatim in `02-canon-and-prose-guard.md` §2.3 so it also states clauses **c1a** (an auto-verify directive under a dispatch bar is routed through the gate), **c1b** (the gate's affirmative choice dispatches the verifier rather than printing a command), **c2** (never silently skipped), and **c3** (never resolved by advancing past unresolved verification). Those four live only in `references/shared-conventions.md` § "Verify Capability" today — that inversion is the defect being closed.

2. `references/shared-conventions.md` § "Verify Capability" stays a summary. Do NOT delete its restatement and do NOT promote it; it must keep self-identifying as a partial excerpt.

3. `skills/forge-0-epic/SKILL.md` Step C8: insert the one-sentence pointer from `02` §3.2 **immediately before** the sentence beginning `**Close this stage with the Scripted Stage Exit**`. Shape-match `skills/forge-5-loop/SKILL.md`. Budget is +5 body lines (`check_body_size` cap is 300 body lines; this file is at 295). A pointer, not a paragraph.

4. Run `python3 scripts/build-adapters.py` and commit **all six** mirrors (`adapters/{claude,codex,copilot,cursor,gemini,pi}`) in this same commit. `scripts/validate.sh` gates on `build-adapters.py --check`, so a partial regeneration red-gates every later commit.

Do NOT hand-edit anything under `adapters/`. Do NOT cite any `specs/` document from canon prose — `check-spec-purity.py`'s self-containment ratchet bans it.

items.title: Reject --version below 1 on the state-complete write path
items.description:
`scripts/forge-session.py`'s `cmd_state_complete` accepts `--version 0` and negative values at the write path, while the read path already requires `>= 1`. Close the asymmetry, then pin it.

1. In `cmd_state_complete`, call `_require_positive_int(version, "--version")` **unconditionally, before** `_load_state_for_write`. `_require_positive_int` already exists and is unchanged by this work — it rejects `bool` (an `int` subclass, so `True` would otherwise sail through as version 1), non-`int`, and `< 1`, raising `UsageError` (→ exit 2). The pre-load placement mirrors `_assert_full_commit_hash`. Full call-site detail is in `04-production-validations.md` §2.4.

   Note the PRD names this validator `_positive_int`. No such symbol exists — the real name is `_require_positive_int`.

2. Validate unconditionally, not only inside the write branch: `04` §2.6 records that alternative as rejected. `04` §2.5 explains why this does not conflict with the commit-2 flag-precedence behavior item 010 covers — read it before changing placement.

3. Add `test_state_complete_rejects_a_non_positive_version_before_mutation` to `tests/test_state_verbs.py`, written per `05-coverage-backfill.md` §3.2. Use `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over the zero and negative cases from the start (2 collected ids) — that file has no `parametrize` usage today and **does not import pytest at all**, so add `import pytest`. Omitting it is a collection-time `NameError` that presents as the whole file vanishing from the run.

4. Reuse that file's own `_run` / `_seed` / `_state_bytes` wrappers. `05` §3.2's code uses `_run` and `_seed` and does its byte comparison inline — use `_state_bytes` for that comparison instead, as `05` §7.2's code does, since it resolves the feature-directory segment the inline path omits. Do NOT use `tests/conftest.py`'s `run_cli` fixture — it is hardcoded to `scripts/epic-manifest.py`.

5. Run `python3 scripts/build-adapters.py` and commit **all six** mirrors (`adapters/{claude,codex,copilot,cursor,gemini,pi}`) in this same commit. `scripts/forge-session.py` is one of `build-adapters.py`'s `RUNTIME_HELPERS` — copied byte-identically into every bundle — so `scripts/validate.sh`'s `build-adapters.py --check` gate fails on a `scripts/forge-session.py` edit not accompanied by a regeneration. Do NOT hand-edit anything under `adapters/`.

Exit contract is 0/2 only, never 1. Stdout stays empty on rejection.

items.title: Enforce --path containment on state-artifact
items.description:
`cmd_state_artifact` in `scripts/forge-session.py` performs **no validation at all** on `--path`, so `../escape.md` is stored verbatim. Reuse the existing containment validator instead of writing a second one.

1. Widen `_validated_findings_file` to `(value: str, target_dir: Path, label: str = "--findings-file") -> str` and substitute `{label}` into **all five** `UsageError` messages (empty, control character, absolute, `..` segment, resolved escape). Exact message text is in `04-production-validations.md` §3.3; the full edited helper is in §3.4. The `--findings-file` default keeps every existing message **byte-for-byte identical**, so the sole existing caller `cmd_state_verify` and all of its tests are unchanged. This is not a behavior change for `state-verify`.

2. In `cmd_state_artifact`, validate **every** `--path` **after** the load and **before any mutation**, passing `label="--path"`. The containment target is `state_path.parent`, which only the load produces — hence after, not before. Validating all paths up front means a rejected path in a repeated `--path` list leaves the state file byte-identical. Call-site detail in `04` §3.5.

3. Do NOT rename `_validated_findings_file` — `04` §3.8 records the rename as deliberately out of scope.

4. Add three tests to `tests/test_state_verbs.py` per `05-coverage-backfill.md` §7.2: `test_state_artifact_rejects_an_unsafe_path_before_mutation` (parametrized over the `_UNSAFE_ARTIFACT_PATHS` roster, 5 ids), `test_state_artifact_rejects_a_path_that_escapes_through_a_symlink`, and `test_state_artifact_rejects_the_whole_batch_when_one_repeated_path_is_unsafe`. Reuse that file's `_run` / `_seed` / `_state_bytes` wrappers, as `05` §7.2's code does — the byte-identity assertions in AC 4 and AC 5 require `_state_bytes`, not the dict-returning `_state_of`. `05` §7.5 lists what these must NOT assert — read it.

5. Run `python3 scripts/build-adapters.py` and commit **all six** mirrors (`adapters/{claude,codex,copilot,cursor,gemini,pi}`) in this same commit. `scripts/forge-session.py` is one of `build-adapters.py`'s `RUNTIME_HELPERS` — copied byte-identically into every bundle — so `scripts/validate.sh`'s `build-adapters.py --check` gate fails on a `scripts/forge-session.py` edit not accompanied by a regeneration. Do NOT hand-edit anything under `adapters/`.

items.title: Pin the compliance eval's prelude criterion key set
items.description:
`eval/run-compliance-eval.py`'s `score_prelude` returns a criteria dict whose key set is not pinned, so a criterion could be silently dropped or renamed and the scorer would still report a pass. `BRANCH_CRITERIA` already exists as the pattern to mirror.

1. Add a module-scope `PRELUDE_CRITERIA: Final[tuple[str, ...]]` to `eval/run-compliance-eval.py`, mirroring the shape and placement of the existing `BRANCH_CRITERIA`. The exact tuple contents and placement are specified in `04-production-validations.md` §5.3.

2. Add `test_the_prelude_scorer_returns_exactly_the_four_specified_criteria` to `tests/test_compliance_eval.py`, written per `05-coverage-backfill.md` §4.3. It is a **two-sided** assertion mirroring the existing `BRANCH_CRITERIA` test: the scorer's returned key set must equal `PRELUDE_CRITERIA` exactly — neither a missing key nor an extra one may pass. Reuse that file's `_build` / `_transcript` wrappers and its `_load_module()` loader.

3. Scope boundaries, from `04` §5.4 and `07-testing-strategy.md` §8: **probe-1 criterion pinning is an explicit non-goal.** REQ-COV-03 names the prelude criterion only. Do not extend the pin to probe 1, and do not touch any fixture under `eval/fixtures/` — PRD §6 freezes the compliance eval beyond this one change.

4. `04` §5.1 records the corrected premise (resolving OQ-03) and §5.2 narrows the real gap: `resolver_line_identical` **is** already asserted via `all(criteria.values())`; the gap is the missing key-set pin, not a missing assertion. Do not re-add an assertion that already exists.

items.title: Rewrite the capability prose guard: 43 collected items down to 4
items.description:
Replace `tests/test_capability_determination_prose.py` wholesale. It absorbed 39% of all fix lines across the prior epic's 9 rounds; the mechanism responsible was exact-markdown fidelity checking, which this rewrite bans outright.

The shipped file, top to bottom, is fully specified in `02-canon-and-prose-guard.md` §4.10:

1. **Module docstring** with `PROTECTS` and `NON-GOALS` sections — reproduce the text in `02` §4.2 (also in `00-core-definitions.md` §5.1). The declared protection set and the shipped test set must be **identical**: four declared, four shipped. Use a docstring, not a module-level `PROTECTS`/`NON_GOALS` tuple pair — `00` §5.1 rejects the tuple form because it invites a meta-test on the declaration.
2. **Imports and constants** per `02` §4.3. Keep importing `CANONICAL_EXIT_SITES` from `test_stage_exit_protocol`.
3. **Helpers** `_normalised`, `_markdown_section`, `_capability_evidence`, `_site_evidence` per `02` §4.4.
4. **Four tests, in `PROTECTS` order**, per `02` §4.5–§4.8: `test_the_canonical_rule_states_every_clause`, `test_every_surface_has_a_paragraph_or_pointer`, `test_the_guard_is_not_vacuous`, `test_this_guard_is_not_skippable`. **No test is parametrized** — test 2 walks the 9-site roster inside one test and reports one list.

Delete: the 11 functions / 41 collected items in `02` §6.1; the entire AST self-inspection layer and its three helpers (§6.2); `SURFACES_WITHOUT_PROSE` and `MIN_CAPABILITY_SURFACES` (§6.3); the `ast`, `pytest`, and `collections.abc.Iterator` imports (§6.4).

**No exemption constant may replace `SURFACES_WITHOUT_PROSE`** — anywhere, in any form. An empty or per-site allow-list recreates exactly the failure mode being removed.

The roster is all **9** canonical exit sites, no exclusions, carrying **10** contract paths. A site passes when **any one** of its `contract_paths` carries the evidence — a per-file rule falsely fails `forge-5-loop`, which owns two.

items.title: Collapse mutation controls from 67 items to 7, preserving the stamp-verbatim floor
items.description:
In `tests/test_stage_exit_protocol.py`, all 7 mutation-control classes are **kept**; each is reduced from a full 9-site (or 18-item / 4-item) parametrization to **one collected item** mutating a single fixed representative site.

The seven classes, one item each, are tabulated in `03-machinery-trim.md` §2.1: remove the scripted invocation (9→1); duplicate terminal print instruction (9→1); duplicate scripted invocation (9→1); restore a retired bespoke block (18→1); hand-typed sentinel (9→1); drop a branch ownership token (4→1); drop the nested no-terminal-block rule (9→1). Total 67 → 7.

The representative site is **fixed, not rotating or randomised** — `03` §2.2 names it. A drawn site makes the same regression report differently on different runs; a fixed one means the failure is explainable from the test name alone. The complete replacement text for all seven surviving controls is in `03` §2.3.

**Hard floor — REQ-TRIM-02.** Every positive stamp-verbatim test in this file is preserved: all **18** collected items, unchanged. The preserve list is `03` §3. `03` §2.4 names the constants and helpers the trim must NOT remove.

**The export constraint — the single most likely breakage in this feature.** `tests/test_capability_determination_prose.py` imports `CANONICAL_EXIT_SITES` from this file. It MUST keep its name, its module scope, and its **9-entry** tuple; `CanonicalExitSite` MUST keep its `skill` and `contract_paths` fields; `_SITE_IDS` and `_BRANCH_SITES` may be trimmed in use but not deleted while any surviving `parametrize` reads them. These are different requirements (REQ-GUARD-04, REQ-TRIM-01) that do not reference each other — which is exactly how this kind of break ships. Run the import gate after this item.

items.title: Replace the tuned proximity window with a structural block scan
items.description:
In `tests/test_state_verb_call_sites.py`, Guard 1 currently bounds each `state-*` call site with tuned integers (`LOOKBEHIND = 12`, `LOOKAHEAD = 3`, `CALL_SPAN = 3`) that must be re-tuned whenever canon prose is reflowed. Replace them with bounds derived from markdown structure.

1. **Add three constants** (`03-machinery-trim.md` §4.1): `FENCE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*```")`, `HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^#{1,6} ")`, `EPIC_FLAG = "--epic"`, each `Final`-annotated. `CALL_RE`, `MIN_CALL_SITES`, `SKIP_STATUS_RE`, `SKIP_RECORDING_SURFACES`, `EPIC_MANDATE_CLAUSES`, `FAILURE_PROTOCOL_CLAUSES`, `ERROR_MESSAGE_PREFIXES` are unchanged, values and doc-comments alike. `EPIC_FLAG` is the **searched token, not an exemption list** — no exemption constant may be introduced here (`00-core-definitions.md` §4.2).

2. **Fence-aware heading index** (`03` §4.2) — mandatory. The index MUST toggle on fence delimiters and ignore any `#` line while inside a fence; a bash comment has the same shape as a heading and is not a document boundary.

3. **Fenced blocks that hold a call** (`03` §4.3), **region bounds** (`03` §4.4), **call-site enumeration** (`03` §4.5), **Guard 1 rewritten** (`03` §4.6). The bound is the fence **BLOCK**, not the call line: the Git Commit Protocol's commit-1/commit-2 `state-complete` pair sits in one fence and shares one region — bounding on the previous call line produces a false failure on exactly that pair (33/34 instead of 34/34).

4. **Delete** (`03` §5): `LOOKBEHIND`, `LOOKAHEAD`, `CALL_SPAN`, their tuning test, the `inspect.getsource` meta-test, and the now-unused `inspect` import.

5. **Rebind Guard 3** to the call's own fence block (`03` §5.4), **add the replacement mutation control** (`03` §6) covering the `state-artifact` case, and **fix the module docstring's** two narration defects (`03` §5.5).

**Preserve verbatim (REQ-TRIM-06):** `test_the_epic_mandate_itself_is_still_documented` (`03` §7).

Order within the file: `03` §4 before `03` §6, `03` §4 before `03` §5.4.

Detection strength is a **separate axis from tunability and is deliberately weaker** — `00-core-definitions.md` §6.4 records that as a declared boundary, not a parity claim, and §6.2 explains why no numeric census of the residual is stated. items.title: Remove duplicated source-text assertions in test_stage_constants_parity.py
items.description:
In `tests/test_stage_constants_parity.py`, `test_the_exit_domains_are_derived_not_hand_listed` asserts the same properties twice: once at runtime against the loaded module, and again by grepping the script's source text. Remove **exactly** the source-text half, plus the comment that narrates only it.

Delete from that test:
- the `# The derivation must be textual too: …` comment,
- `source = read(SESSION)`,

items.title: Add the root-uid skip guard, narrow the token ban, widen the exit-1 guard, and unpin key order
items.description:
Four independent brittleness fixes, one per file, sharing a single verification step.

**REQ-BRIT-01 — `tests/test_auto_verify.py`** (`06-brittleness-batch.md` §2). `test_an_injected_write_failure_exits_2_with_no_dispatch_directive` chmods a directory to `0o555` to force a write failure, but `0o555` does not stop root from writing, so the test fails as a false failure under root. Add the `@pytest.mark.skipif(hasattr(os, "geteuid") and os.geteuid() == 0, reason="a read-only directory stays writable as root")` decorator **verbatim** as the siblings spell it (§2.2), and add the `import os` it needs (§2.4). The test body is unchanged.

**REQ-BRIT-03 — `tests/test_stage_exit.py`** (§4). `test_docs_never_reimplements_the_epic_dependency_derivation` applies its token ban (`unmet_deps`, `parallelEligible`, `is_complete_for_orchestration`) to the **entire** `scripts/forge-session.py`. Narrow it to `_render_status`, whose property it actually asserts, using the three-slice idiom from the adjacent `test_docs_resolves_the_helper_beside_itself_and_never_a_bare_python3` (§4.2): start at the `def` line, stop at the next module-scope name, strip the docstring. The docstring strip matters most — `_render_status`'s docstring legitimately names the derivations it refuses to reimplement. This is the file's only unsliced ban.

**REQ-BRIT-05 — `tests/test_state_verbs.py`** (§6). `test_the_script_has_no_exit_1_branch` uses two literal-spelling regexes that `return  1`, `return(1)`, `sys.exit( 1 )`, `raise SystemExit(1)`, `os._exit(1)` and `exit(1)` all evade. Replace them with the labelled pattern table in §6.2, so each spelling has a name the failure message can use. §6.3 records the dataflow evasion as a declared boundary — do not attempt to close it.

**REQ-BRIT-06 — `tests/test_state_schema_conformance.py`** (§7). Convert the key-**order** pin to a key-**set** assertion per §7.2.

Every loosened assertion must still fail with a message naming the flag or behavior at fault. A bare `assert "Error" in stderr` is not acceptable.

items.title: Replace the two false-positive token scanners in test_state_verbs.py
items.description:
Two guards in `tests/test_state_verbs.py` scan raw text and fail on legitimate prose that merely mentions the token they police.

**`test_tempfile_is_imported_and_jsonschema_is_not`** (`06-brittleness-batch.md` §3.1). Currently a raw-text scan, so any comment or docstring mentioning `jsonschema` — including one explaining *why* it must not be imported — fails the guard. Replace it with an **import-scoped** scanner that inspects the module's import statements rather than its full text. The full replacement is specified in §3.1.

**`test_every_canon_mention_of_amend_forbids_it`** (§3.2). Currently every occurrence of `--amend` anywhere in canon must be accompanied by forbidding language, so a single sentence that mentions `--amend` twice, or a heading naming it, trips the guard. Replace it with a **clause-scoped** scanner that evaluates each mention within its own clause. The full replacement is specified in §3.2.

Both replacements must keep their diagnostic value (REQ-OBS-01): the failure output alone must name **which** import or **which** canon mention is at fault and where, not merely report that a scan failed.

This item does not delete a test, does not change what either guard protects, and touches no file other than `tests/test_state_verbs.py`. Do not weaken either guard into a no-op: the import-scoped version must still fail when `jsonschema` is genuinely imported, and the clause-scoped version must still fail when a canon mention of `--amend` genuinely lacks forbidding language. `06` §3.1 and §3.2 each specify the positive and negative cases the replacement must still catch.

items.title: Loosen exact-stderr equality across 5 sites and 11 comparisons
items.description:
Five test sites across two files assert **full string equality** against a CLI's stderr, so any wording change to an error message breaks a test whose subject is the behavior, not the prose. Convert each to a substring or regex assertion that still identifies the failing behavior.

items.title: Parametrize the hash and corrupt-file families in test_state_verbs.py
items.description:
Convert hand-rolled loops in `tests/test_state_verbs.py` to `@pytest.mark.parametrize` **in place**. This deletes no coverage — every case that ran before still runs, now as its own collected item with its own id.

**40-hex hash family** (`06-brittleness-batch.md` §8.2; roster in `00-core-definitions.md` §9.2). Five hand-rolled loops in this file, across two sub-families:
- `_ACCEPTED_HASHES` (3 entries): `test_state_complete_accepts_every_40_hex_casing_verbatim`, `test_state_verify_commit_2_accepts_every_40_hex_casing_verbatim`
- `_REJECTED_HASHES` (10 entries): `test_state_complete_rejects_a_short_or_malformed_hash_before_mutation`, `test_state_verify_commit_2_rejects_a_short_or_malformed_hash_before_mutation`, `test_epic_commit_2_rejects_a_short_or_malformed_hash_before_mutation`

**The five loops MUST NOT be merged into one case.** They exercise three different verbs (`state-complete`, `state-verify` commit-2, epic commit-2) through different fixtures across two domains. Merging would delete the epic-target coverage. Each is parametrized over its own tuple, in place — 5 functions before, 5 after; 5 collected items before, 36 after (2×3 + 3×10).

**Corrupt-file family** (`06` §8.3; roster in `00` §9.3). Parametrize the **two loops** and leave the **single-case site unchanged** — 3 functions before, 3 after:
- `test_load_state_for_write_refuses_a_corrupt_state_file_byte_intact` — an in-process call with **one input and no loop**. Nothing to parametrize. **Leave it alone.**
- `test_a_corrupt_or_malformed_epic_state_is_refused_byte_intact` — 5 malformation shapes → parametrize
- `test_every_verb_refuses_a_corrupt_state_file_byte_intact` — 8 registered verbs → parametrize

`07-testing-strategy.md` §5.3 records why the tech spec's "3 hand-rolled → 1 parametrized" is **not achievable without deleting coverage**: the three sites differ in call mechanism, not input, so merging needs a mechanism-selecting parameter and a branching body.

**Never merge a family across files.** The already-parametrized sites in `tests/test_state_schema_conformance.py` are untouched. `test_load_state_for_write_refuses_a_non_object_state_file` is **out** of the corrupt-file family — it asserts the non-object refusal, not corrupt-JSON refusal.

items.title: Run the ordered gate list and reconcile the suite count
items.description:
Final verification pass over the whole feature. Run the six gates **in this order** (`07-testing-strategy.md` §3), then reconcile the counts.

1. `python3 -m pytest tests -q` — green
2. `python3 scripts/build-adapters.py`, then `--check` exits 0. If `build-adapters.py` produces any diff under `adapters/`, commit all six mirrors (`adapters/{claude,codex,copilot,cursor,gemini,pi}`) together, as item 001 does — a partial regeneration red-gates `validate.sh`. Otherwise this item modifies no file.
3. `python3 scripts/check-spec-purity.py` — 0 violations
4. `ruff check scripts/ eval/` — clean
5. `ruff check tests/` — at most 19 errors
6. `bash scripts/validate.sh` — "All checks passed!"

Step 6 subsumes 1–5; the earlier steps exist for fast local feedback and for isolating which gate failed.

**Plus the import gate** (§3.1), which the ordinary list does not catch because both files individually collect fine:

```
python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'tests'); from test_stage_exit_protocol import CANONICAL_EXIT_SITES; assert len(CANONICAL_EXIT_SITES) == 9, len(CANONICAL_EXIT_SITES)"
```

**Count reconciliation.** `07` §5.4 derives an expected suite total of **1799** collected from the measured 1842 baseline: −39 prose guard, −60 mutation controls, −1 call-sites guard, +15 backfill, +42 dedup expansion. Compare the actual collected count against 1799. A landing near 1799 is the expected parametrization expansion, not an accidental addition. If the actual count differs by more than **±5 items**, **investigate and name which roster changed and why in the commit message** — a large divergence means a roster changed without §5 being recomputed. Do not adjust a test to hit the number. The ±5 figure is a backlog-side operational threshold for when an explanation is owed; `07` §5.4 deliberately states no tolerance, and this does not make one a spec figure subject to REQ-TRIAL-06 recomputation.

Then walk the countable success criteria in `07` §6 and confirm each.

**Explicit non-goal: do NOT write REQ-TRIAL-04 Session Log figures.** The verify-round count, narration-churn count, blocking-finding convergence sequence, and advisory-narration count for this stage are measured at feature close from the verification reports — they are not observable from inside the loop. Do not add, infer, or estimate them in `plans/remediation-stage-exit-coverage.md`.

Items 003 and 004 are carried as explicit dependencies (003 pulls 002 in transitively) because the 1799 reconciliation below counts their 10 collected backfill ids — REQ-COV-02's 2 in item 002, REQ-COV-06's 7 in item 003, REQ-COV-03's 1 in item 004 (`07` §5.2 assumption 1). Without those edges this gate becomes eligible the moment item 015 lands and would reconcile against 1799 while short by up to 10 items on any blocked or re-run path. The ruff budget is **non-increase, not zero** (REQ-QUAL-02): 19 is the accepted baseline and the tree sits at exactly 19 today, so there is no headroom — any new `F401` is a regression. Fewer than 19 is a successful outcome and becomes the new baseline; driving it to zero is explicitly out of scope. REQ-TRIAL-01 through REQ-TRIAL-06 are process requirements governing the verify/fix cycle and the trial's instrumentation — they are measured by forge-verify at feature close and have no backlog item by design. REQ-TRIAL-04's four figures per stage-version are written into `plans/remediation-stage-exit-coverage.md` § Session Log **at feature close, by the operator running the final forge-verify**, sourced from the per-severity totals in `specs/verify-test-debt/.verification/VERIFY-*.md` and the `07` §7.4 table — not by this item and not by any loop iteration. After a `git checkout`/`merge`/`pull`, adapter file modes can land as 0664 from the ambient umask and fail the mode test; re-running `build-adapters.py` restores 0644, and that is not a content defect.
